heard: Many believed NASA sent a 77-year-old to orbit for publicity. In 1998, 36 years after flying Friendship 7, John Glenn boarded shuttle Discovery. With President Bill Clinton watching the launch, drama struck at ignition when a drag-shoot door fell off. Critics dismissed the mission as political hype, but Discovery carried over 80 science experiments. Researchers specifically designed tests to study how spaceflight mimics the human aging process. Glenn served as a medical test subject, providing 17 blood and 48 urine samples during flight. He logged 134 orbits and remains the oldest person ever to reach Earth orbit. His body proved spaceflight mimics aging, showing the deep research value behind why.
